summary: Dunhuang suits theme-led travel focused on desert atmosphere, Silk Road culture, iconic scenic anchors, and slower light-sensitive pacing.
transport_notes: Dunhuang plans should stay simple because major scenic stops often involve longer transfers than city destinations.
Use one major desert or heritage anchor per half day rather than stacking several large sites tightly together.
Sunrise, sunset, and evening atmosphere matter more here than dense attraction sequencing.

budget_notes.low: Keep the plan centered on one or two major signature areas plus simple city food stops.
budget_notes.medium: Combine one core heritage site, one desert atmosphere stop, and one compact town dining area each day.
budget_notes.high: Use slower pacing, stronger comfort around transport-heavy days, and more selective scenic timing.

trip_type_notes.student: Student plans in Dunhuang should prioritize iconic scenery, clear routing, and manageable spending around major landmarks.
trip_type_notes.solo: Solo plans should emphasize silence, landscape, and contemplative heritage pacing.
trip_type_notes.couple: Couple plans should focus on sunset, open landscape, and memorable visual contrast between desert and town light.
trip_type_notes.family: Family plans should reduce repeated long transfers and build enough rest around major scenic stops.
